title: Pazia tuzo ya Mwalimu Nyerere lafunguliwa
content:
Pazia tuzo ya Mwalimu Nyerere lafunguliwa
Muktasari:
- Serikali imefungua dirisha la duru ya tano ya tuzo ya Taifa ya Mwalimu Nyerere ya uandishi bunifu, huku washindi wakitarajiwa kutangazwa na kukabidhiwa tuzo Aprili 13, 2027.
Tanga. Serikali imezindua dirisha la kuwasilisha miswada kwa ajili ya duru ya tano ya tuzo ya Taifa ya Mwalimu Nyerere ya uandishi bunifu, hatua inayolenga kuhamasisha uandishi, usomaji na ukuzaji wa Kiswahili nchini na nje ya Tanzania.
Akizungumza wakati wa uzinduzi huo leo, Agosti 19, 2026, Waziri wa Elimu, Sayansi na Teknolojia, Profesa Adolf Mkenda, amesema dirisha hilo limezinduliwa rasmi, huku washindi wakitarajiwa kutangazwa na kukabidhiwa tuzo Aprili 13, 2027, siku ya kumbukumbu ya kuzaliwa kwa Mwalimu Julius Nyerere.
Profesa Mkenda amesema mshindi wa kila nyanja atapata Sh10 milioni, huku kazi yake ikichapishwa na kusambazwa kwa gharama za Serikali, akisisitiza kuwa hatua hiyo inalenga kuwapa waandishi motisha na fursa ya kutambulika kitaifa.
“Lengo ni kuhakikisha waandishi wanapata fursa ya kuandika na kutambulika, huku vitabu vyao vikisomwa na wananchi wengi zaidi,” amesema Profesa Mkenda.
Amesema tuzo hiyo, iliyoanzishwa mwaka 2022/2023, inasimamiwa na kamati huru ya tuzo inayoongozwa na Profesa Penina Mlama, ikiwa na wajumbe Dk Aikande Mkwai, Profesa Ally Mcharazo, Esta Mngolo na Dk Salma Hamad, ambao wanafanya kazi kwa uhuru kutoka maeneo mbalimbali.
Kwa mujibu wa Profesa Mkenda, tuzo hiyo inalenga pia kukuza Kiswahili kupitia maandishi, kuongeza usomaji wa vitabu, kuchangamsha soko la uchapishaji na kuhifadhi utamaduni pamoja na historia ya Tanzania kupitia kazi za fasihi.
“Tanzania inahitaji kuwa na vitabu vingi vinavyoelezea utamaduni na historia yetu, kwa sababu usipoielezea nchi yako, wengine wataielezea,” amesema, akitoa mfano wa namna vitabu vya fasihi vinavyoweza kusaidia kuelewa jamii na utamaduni wa nchi mbalimbali.
Amesema tangu kuanzishwa kwa tuzo hiyo, zaidi ya miswada 1,300 imewasilishwa na aina sita za vitabu vilivyoshinda tayari zimechapishwa na kusambazwa shuleni na maktaba, huku jumla ya nakala 292,000 zikisambazwa katika shule za msingi na sekondari nchini.
Kwa upande wake, mwenyekiti wa kamati huru ya tuzo, Profesa Penina Mlama, amesema dirisha la kuwasilisha miswada limefunguliwa leo, Agosti 19, na litakuwa wazi hadi Novemba 30, 2026, likiwapa waandishi muda wa miezi mitatu kuwasilisha kazi zao.
Profesa Mlama amesema mshiriki anatakiwa kuwa raia wa Tanzania, aandike kazi kwa Kiswahili, awasilishe andiko moja katika nyanja atakayoichagua na kuhakikisha muswada huo haujawahi kuchapishwa mahali popote.
“Waandishi wanatakiwa kusaini tamko maalumu kuthibitisha kuwa kazi wanayowasilisha ni yao na haijawahi kuchapishwa mahali popote,” amesema Profesa Mlama, akisisitiza kuwa miswada iliyowahi kushika nafasi ya kwanza hadi ya kumi hairuhusiwi kurudiwa, ingawa mwandishi anaweza kuwasilisha muswada mwingine.
Amesema mshindi wa kwanza atapata Sh10 milioni na kuchapishiwa kazi yake kwa gharama za Serikali, mshindi wa pili atapata Sh7 milioni na cheti, huku mshindi wa tatu akipata Sh5 milioni na cheti.

title: Programul „Euro 200” 2026: Elevii și studenții primesc bonurile valorice din 31 august. Până când pot cumpăra calculatoare
content:
Programul „Euro 200” intră în etapa acordării bonurilor valorice și a achiziționării calculatoarelor. În acest an, 2.339 de elevi și studenți incluși pe lista aprobată de Ministerul Educației și Cercetării beneficiază de sprijinul financiar în valoare de 200 de euro. Guvernul a adoptat joi, 20 august, hotărârea prin care este stabilit modelul documentului ce va fi utilizat în 2026.
Ajutorul nu este oferit în numerar, ci prin intermediul unui bon care poate fi folosit pentru cumpărarea unui calculator personal nou, în condițiile stabilite prin legislația programului.
Când vor fi eliberate bonurile valorice „Euro 200”
Documentele vor ajunge la persoanele eligibile în perioada 31 august-11 septembrie 2026, conform calendarului aprobat prin Ordinul ministrului Educației și Cercetării nr. 3.616/2026. Înaintea acestei etape, ministerul le achiziționează și le distribuie inspectoratelor școlare și instituțiilor de învățământ superior.
Beneficiarii vor putea cumpăra echipamentele între 7 septembrie și 16 octombrie. Cele două intervale se suprapun, ceea ce înseamnă că elevii și studenții care intră mai devreme în posesia documentului îl pot utiliza după începerea perioadei rezervate achizițiilor.
Ulterior, copiile facturilor și ale proceselor-verbale de predare-primire trebuie depuse până la 30 octombrie, potrivit calendarului oficial. Decontarea sumelor către operatorii economici se va desfășura până la 27 noiembrie.
Cine beneficiază de ajutorul de 200 de euro
Programul este destinat elevilor și studenților în vârstă de până la 26 de ani, înscriși în învățământul de stat sau particular acreditat și proveniți din familii cu venituri reduse. Plafonul luat în calcul este de maximum 500 de lei venit brut lunar pentru fiecare membru al familiei.
- Principala noutate introdusă este aceea că venitul brut lunar pe membru de familie a fost majorat de la 250 de lei la 500 de lei, urmare a evoluției indicelui prețului de consum comunicat de Institutul Național de Statistică.
Ajutorul nu este oferit în numerar, ci prin intermediul unui bon care poate fi folosit pentru cumpărarea unui calculator personal nou, în condițiile stabilite prin legislația programului.
Lista aferentă anului 2026 a fost aprobată prin Ordinul ministrului Educației și Cercetării nr. 4.157/2026. Prin urmare, bonurile care urmează să fie distribuite nu pot fi solicitate de alte persoane în această etapă, ci revin exclusiv celor 2.339 de beneficiari selectați în urma procedurii derulate anterior.
Ce echipamente pot fi cumpărate prin programul „Euro 200”
Configurația minimă recomandată a calculatoarelor pentru achiziționarea cărora se acordă sprijinul financiar este următoarea:
a) pentru desktop: procesor cu frecvență nominală minimum 3.0 GHz, HDD minimum 500 GB sau SSD minim 240 GB, RAM tip DDR3 sau DDR4 minimum 8 GB, monitor LCD sau LED cu diagonală minimum 18.5“ și rezoluție minimum 1920 x 1080, tastatură, mouse optic, cameră WEB;
b) pentru laptop sau notebook, ultrabook sau dispozitive echivalente: procesor cu minimum 2 nuclee, RAM tip DDR3 sau DDR4 minimum 8 GB, HDD minimum 500 GB sau SSD minimum 240GB, diagonală minimum 14“, rezoluție minimum 1.366 x 768, cameră WEB.
Ajutorul reprezintă echivalentul în lei al sumei de 200 de euro, fără a putea depăși prețul calculatorului cumpărat. Dacă produsul ales este mai scump decât valoarea înscrisă pe bon, diferența va fi suportată de beneficiar.
Editor : C.S.

title: Après l’incendie dans les Hautes Fagnes, plusieurs routes rouvrent ce mardi : voici ce qui change
content:
Après l'incendie dans les Hautes Fagnes, plusieurs routes rouvrent ce mardi : voici ce qui change
Après plusieurs jours de fortes restrictions, un premier retour à la normale se profile dans la région.
- Publié le 24-08-2026 à 18h30
- Mis à jour le 24-08-2026 à 18h32
Après une dizaine de jours de fermeture à la suite de l'incendie qui s'est déclaré le 14 août dans les Fagnes, la circulation pourra reprendre ce mardi dès 10h00 sur la N676, la N672 et la N68, indiquent les services du gouverneur de la province. L'accès aux Fagnes reste cependant interdit, insistent-ils.
L'arrêt et le stationnement resteront interdits sur ces axes aux abords du sinistre et la vitesse y sera limitée à 50 km/h.
Cette réouverture permettra aux commerces et établissements dont l'activité était entravée par les restrictions de circulation de reprendre normalement leurs activités.
La réouverture de ces routes ne signifie toutefois pas la réouverture des Hautes Fagnes, soulignent les services de la province. L'accès au site reste strictement interdit, tant pour la sécurité des citoyens que pour celle des intervenants.

title: The first Navajo NFL player just gave a locker room speech even rival fans are praising
content:
NFL players are an incredibly diverse bunch. Today, there are Samoan players and Australian players, as well as players from Guinea and Nigeria and Cameroon. Still, most rosters in the league are overwhelmingly American.
Yet there’s one kind of American that has never before been signed to an NFL team: Navajo. That is, until now.
First Navajo NFL player makes his debut
Shiyazh Tastohyinya Pete was a standout offensive tackle for New Mexico State and Kentucky. But even as a massive and talented player, his odds for the NFL were a longshot.
Not only was the 6-foot-9-inch player viewed as a fringe draft prospect, but he is also a proud member of the Navajo Nation. Pete had history working against him: No Navajo had ever been signed or played in the NFL before.
Though he went unselected in the draft, the Dallas Cowboys reached out shortly afterwards and offered him a free agent contract. Together, they made history.
On August 15, Pete made his NFL preseason debut in a game against the Seattle Seahawks. The following week, he played much closer to home when the Cowboys took on the Arizona Cardinals.
Stunningly, thousands of members of the Navajo Nation showed up to demonstrate their support for Pete, including the nation’s President, Buu Nygren.
After his brief but historic performance and a Cowboys win, head coach Brian Schottenheimer asked Pete to address the team in the locker room following the game.
“I saw something tonight I’ve never seen before [in] 25 years in the NFL,” Schottenheimer marveled. “An entire section cheering for one man.”
Pete speaks after historic debut
“That was an incredible win. I am very fortunate to be amongst you and to play on the same field, wear the same star on our chest,” he said to his teammates. “I’m proud of us, proud of how far we’ve come. Fate brought us here as strangers, but this star, this team, will make us brothers.”
Of course, Pete is talking about football. He’s proud of the accomplishments of the team and their loyalty to one another.
But it’s not hard to see that his words also paint a much bigger picture.
Pete’s clip has gone viral across YouTube and social media, with commenters in awe of his journey:
“You can literally hear our ancestors in his voice. That speech is so powerful!”
“That man speaks with earned wisdom. What an incredible voice for his people.”
“He won the team, the fans and the country over with just a few heat felt words! Well [done] young man!”
“Congratulation to Pete! Congratulation to the NFL and Congratulation to America, showing that we are still growing towards more greatness”
As for Pete, when asked later what he saw when he looked up at the crowd of several thousand Navajo giving him a standing ovation, he simply said, “Hope. Courage.”
A massive man and a massive win for native representation
It’s hard to overstate how meaningful it is to see Pete take the field in a Dallas Cowboys uniform. The Cowboys are widely regarded as America’s team, the blue star completely synonymous with classic Americana.
Representation of Native Americans in American media and institutions has, for decades, been subpar. They’ve been the enemy (Cowboys vs Indians), the stereotype (the Washington Redskins), or completely invisible. There are over 400,000 enrolled members of the Navajo, with a little less than half of them living on the reservation where they’ve chosen to maintain their own sovereignty. Pete’s journey, his speech, and his viral moment might just show young Navajo that there is a place for them to be accepted and celebrated in American culture, if they want it.
For example, one mother told CBS News that her son had been bullied for wearing a braid in his hair, as per Navajo tradition, and that it meant the world to him to see Pete take the field doing the same. And that’s just the beginning.
“Now he’s got a line of small boys that are ready to take the challenge and be able to say, ‘Hey, I’m right behind you,’” she said.

Na atualidade internacional, um drone que entrou no espaço aéreo da Romênia hoje de madrugada, foi abatido.
Foi abatido por um caça espanhol em missão no país membro da NATO, anunciou o ministro romeno da Defesa. O drone tinha chegado da vizinha Moldávia, foi interceptado por um avião F-18. O ministério reportou a possível queda de destroços numa zona desabitada da região de Galati, perto da fronteira com a Ucrânia. A Romênia tornou-se um dos membros da NATO mais exposto às consequências da guerra na Ucrânia. A costa oriental do país encontra-se próxima de zonas regularmente alvo de ataques aéreos russos.
E esta madrugada, Luís, há registro de mais uma troca de ataques entre Rússia e Ucrânia.
Foram ouvidas explosões em Kiev. Na rede social Telegram, o autarca da capital ucraniana anunciou que a cidade estava debaixo de um ataque de mísseis balísticos e, por isso, aconselhou a população de Kiev a ficar em casa. A administração militar da capital reporta um incêndio num edifício não residencial, num dos distritos, depois do ataque russo. Do lado do Kremlin, as defesas antiaéreas abateram pelo menos 38 drones que ameaçavam a Rússia durante a madrugada. Foi o que adiantou o presidente da Câmara de Moscovo.
Vamos ao futebol. O jogo que estava previsto para hoje entre Sporting de Braga e Gil Vicente foi adiado, Luís.
Isto por causa de um surto gastrointestinal que está a afetar grande parte da equipa bracarense, é o que adianta a Liga Portugal em comunicado. O jogo da segunda jornada do campeonato entre o Sporting de Braga e Gil Vicente estava marcado para hoje, às 08h30 no Estádio Municipal de Braga, mas fica adiado para uma data ainda a combinar entre os dois clubes. A Liga acrescenta no comunicado que este adiamento foi estabelecido por comum acordo entre as duas equipas.
E ontem o Futebol Clube do Porto venceu o Rio Ave por 2 x 0, no Estádio dos Arcos.
Com os dragões a fazerem seis pontos em duas jornadas, a fazerem o pleno. Depois desta vitória dos dragões em Vila do Conde, o treinador portista Francesco Farioli diz estar feliz pela vitória, mas admite que o Porto ainda tem muito para melhorar.
Temos de continuar a trabalhar para alcançar resultados importantes. Há muitos pontos a melhorar. Viemos aqui, sabemos que não era um campo fácil para jogar contra outra equipa que impõe muita força física, muito bem organizada. Por isso, acho que certamente poderíamos ter gerido melhor alguns momentos, mas mais uma vez, tivemos boa eficiência e o resultado é, sem dúvida, o mais importante.
O treinador do Porto, Francesco Farioli, satisfeito depois da vitória por 2 x 0 do Porto frente ao Rio Ave.
O triunfo dos Dragões é um dos temas em destaque no "E o Campeão É?" desta manhã. É para ouvir depois da síntese das 11h30. Ainda no desporto, mas no atletismo, Pedro Pablo Pichardo sagrou-se ontem vice-campeão europeu de triplo salto.
O atleta português conseguiu a medalha de prata na final, depois de saltar 17 metros e 76 centímetros logo ao primeiro ensaio. Apesar de ter atingido a melhor marca pessoal da temporada, o atleta luso-cubano ficou atrás do italiano Andy Diaz, que saltou mais de 18 metros. No final da prova, Pedro Pablo Pichardo assegurou que o foco agora é marcar presença nos próximos Jogos Olímpicos em Los Angeles.
Vamos a tentar fazer de tudo para chegarmos aos Jogos Olímpicos, Los Angeles. Acredito que vou chegar. Mas vamos ver o corpo como se comporta. Hoje, por acaso, senti umas dores no tendão do nada. Não sei se fiz um mau apoio ou já são os anos no triplo também. Não sei, mas vamos tentar chegar a Los Angeles.
Pedro Pablo Pichardo, depois da medalha de prata ontem nos Europeus de Atletismo. É a segunda medalha para Portugal em Birmingham, depois do bronze de Fatuma Tadialo nos 400 metros barreiras. Entretanto, já terminou a primeira prova dos Europeus hoje, a maratona. Na prova feminina, a atleta Vanessa Carvalho foi a melhor das portuguesas. Terminou em 24º lugar, a 13 minutos da campeã. Na maratona masculina, Carlos Costa foi o único representante português e não foi além do 48º lugar.
Nove minutos para lá das 11h, Luís. Vamos a outras notícias que marcam a atualidade.
Na Hungria, pelo menos 12 pessoas morreram num acidente de autocarro esta madrugada. Há ainda 20 feridos. O autocarro de origem polaca caiu numa valeta. A polícia acredita que o motorista terá adormecido, provocando o acidente. O condutor já foi detido. A cidade de Granada registou cerca de 20 réplicas durante a última madrugada, na sequência do sismo de magnitude 5, que abalou ontem esta região do sul de Espanha. A agência de notícias espanhola EFE explica que as réplicas tiveram entre 1,5 e 3,1 de magnitude. Não há registo de vítimas, nem de danos.

title: 김해시, '폭염 안전지도' 농업 전 분야 확대…가공·유통도 관리
content:
(김해=연합뉴스) 이준영 기자 = 경남 김해시는 폭염 장기화에 대응해 농작물 생산현장에 집중했던 '폭염 안전지도'를 농산물 가공·유통 등 농업 전 분야로 확대한다고 18일 밝혔다.
시는 그동안 농작물 생산현장을 중심으로 폭염 피해 예방활동을 벌였으나, 폭염이 장기화하면서 농산물 가공과 선별·포장, 유통·상하차 등 농업과 연계된 전 과정으로 관리 범위를 넓혔다.
생산 단계에서는 비닐하우스와 과수원 등 고온 환경에서 장시간 작업하며 발생할 수 있는 온열질환 예방을 위해 한낮 작업 자제와 충분한 휴식·수분 섭취 등을 안내하고 환기·차광시설 작동 여부를 점검한다.
가공 단계에서는 시설 내부의 높은 온도와 증기, 가공 기계에서 발생하는 열로 인한 온열질환과 화상 위험을 살피고 냉방·환기시설 사용에 따른 전기 과부하와 화재 예방수칙도 안내한다
유통 단계에서는 농산물 선별·포장과 상·하차 작업 과정에서 발생할 수 있는 온열질환과 안전사고 예방에 중점을 둔다.
시는 5개 점검반을 편성해 폭염 취약 현장을 방문하고 농업인과 관련 사업장 종사자에게 폭염 행동 요령을 안내할 계획이다.
특히 시설하우스 등 고온 작업환경에서는 차량 방송 장비를 활용해 한낮 작업 중지를 안내하는 가두방송을 하고 현장 순찰을 통해 안전 수칙 준수 여부도 확인한다.

title: « La Route », sur Arte.tv : dans les vallées isolées de l’Himalaya, la Zanskar Highway bouleverse l’ancien monde
content:
ARTE.TV – À LA DEMANDE – DOCUMENTAIRE
« Avant la route, c’était le bonheur. On prenait le temps. » En 2018, pour sécuriser le nord de son territoire, voisin du Pakistan et de la Chine, New Delhi a décidé de faire sortir des contreforts de l’Himalaya la Zanskar Highway : 298 kilomètres de bitume qui serpentent entre 3 800 mètres et 5 000 mètres d’altitude pour relier Nimmoo, au Ladakh, à Darcha, dans l’Himachal Pradesh. Achevée en mars 2024, elle permet de traverser ces vallées enclavées, parmi les plus pauvres de l’Inde, en seulement trois heures et demie au lieu de six jours auparavant. Beaucoup ont travaillé à la construction de cette route. A la dynamite et aux tractopelles hydrauliques, les hommes. A la pioche et au déblayage à mains nues, les femmes. Six jours sur sept, de 8 heures à 17 heures.
L’anthropologue et réalisatrice Marianne Chaud, éprise de la région au point de l’avoir habitée durant douze ans et d’en avoir appris la langue, filme cette tâche titanesque et inégale, le basculement de tout un ancien monde dans la modernité. Car, même si les smartphones ont déjà gagné chaque foyer, Dechen, Lhamo et Norbu savent que plus rien ne sera jamais plus comme avant. « C’est un vrai progrès, juge Tashi, tisserand et doyen du village. Avec la route arrive le confort. Avant, on ne trouvait rien ici. On mangeait de l’orge et c’est tout. Ils sont tous heureux pour le moment. Ils s’achètent plein de choses. Mais ils vont se jalouser les uns les autres, ils ne pourront plus vivre en paix. »

title: Varsler andre om fare

Smart Volvo-funksjon: Varsler andre om fare
Nå ruller Volvo ut oppdateringer til flere av sine biler.
(Elbil24): Volvos Connected Safety-system har eksistert siden 2016 og får nå en betydelig oppgradering.
Tidligere har systemet kun formidlet varsler om glatt veibane og kjøretøy som bruker nødblink, men med den siste programvareoppdateringen utvides dette til et bredere spekter av trafikkfarer. Oppdateringen gjelder modellene ES90, EX90 og EX60.
Dyr, mennesker, veiarbeid …
Når en av disse bilene oppdager en risiko, som større dyr langs veibanen, fotgjengere eller syklister på motorvei, veiarbeid eller trafikkulykker, sendes posisjonsdataene til Volvo sine servere og deretter videre til andre Volvomodeller i nærheten.
Dermed vil andre førere få opp varsel om at det for eksempel er observert elg i veibanen lenger framme.
Årsaken til at det bare er disse tre modellene som utstyres med teknologien, er at de har den tilstrekkelige datakraften for å behandle informasjonen fra kameraer og sensorer i bilene.
Varselene er ikke bare begrenset til Volvos biler – de sendes også til det europeiske Data for road safety-systemet, slik at de kan deles med kjøretøy fra andre produsenter og veitrafikksentraler.
– Disse innovasjonene bygger på flere tiår med kunnskap fra virkelige trafikkulykker og er enda et steg på veien mot vår visjon om null kollisjoner. Hver gang en Volvo deler sikkerhetsinformasjon, kan det hjelpe andre sjåfører med å oppdage farer tidligere, unngå ulykker og føle seg tryggere på veien, sier Åsa Haglund, leder for Volvo Cars Safety Centre.

Oppdateringen som sendes ut gir også såkalt spatial audio via Apple Carplay. Spatial audio med Dolby Atmos gir mer dybde og større detaljrikdom i lydbildet.
Det forutsetter at man har en bil med Bowers & Wilkins-lydanlegget med 25 høyttalere, som er ekstrautstyr.

Appen analyserer kjørestilen og gir konkrete tilbakemeldinger for å forbedre kjørevaner, og ved å dele disse dataene med forsikringsselskapet Volvia, kan man få lavere forsikringspremie i tråd med hvor trygt man anses å kjøre.

title: Hong Kong lowers heat stress warning system thresholds after calls for revamp
content:
Hong Kong lowers heat stress warning system thresholds after calls for revamp
Labour Department says updates include automatically raising alert level when temperatures in multiple parts of the city reach 35 degrees Celsius
Hong Kong labour authorities have unveiled changes to the system that sends out warnings to workers about overexertion during very hot weather, reducing thresholds so higher-tier alerts can be issued more easily following intense criticism of the mechanism.
The Labour Department said on Thursday that two new conditions would be introduced to the Heat Stress at Work Warning system from Friday.
The system has three warning levels – amber, red and black – which alert employers and staff to the severity of heat stress if they are working outdoors or indoors without air conditioning.
The first change will reduce the threshold for triggering a higher-tier warning if the Observatory has already issued the extremely hot weather special alert, to ensure a quicker response.
The second change will see the warning automatically be raised by one level – from amber to red, or from red to black – when the measured temperatures generally over Hong Kong reach 35 degrees Celsius (95 Fahrenheit) or above.
The revamp was introduced after the system faced criticism over the lack of higher alerts earlier this month, when the city was grappling with record-breaking temperatures.

title: Un défi "énorme": à un mois de la visite du pape, l'Église poursuit les préparatifs pour répondre à l'engouement
content:
Un défi "énorme": à un mois de la visite du pape, l'Église poursuit les préparatifs pour répondre à l'engouement
Des inscriptions prises d'assaut, des milliers de bénévoles et des jeunes déjà au rendez-vous: la visite de Léon XIV suscite un "engouement" qui ravit l’Église de France, en pleins préparatifs à un mois de l'arrivée du pape.
"Non seulement le Stade de France est complet mais nous avons déjà 400.000 inscrits pour la messe du 26 septembre place de la Concorde", à Paris, s'est réjoui dans le journal La Tribune Mgr Benoît Bertrand, le président du comité d'organisation du voyage apostolique prévu du 25 au 28 septembre.
Le défi logistique est énorme pour cette visite qui passera par Paris, Lourdes et Metz. À Paris, elle commencera le vendredi 25 par une rencontre avec le président de la République, Emmanuel Macron, suivi dans l'après-midi, d'une visite à l'Unesco.
Léon XIV se rendra ensuite en papamobile jusqu'à la cathédrale Notre-Dame, qu'il sera le premier pape à visiter depuis sa réouverture en décembre 2024, pour des vêpres réservées au clergé.
Suivra ensuite une grande veillée pour les jeunes (de 17 à 35 ans), le vendredi soir au Stade de France de Saint-Denis, mais les 80.000 places sont, selon le diocèse de Paris, parties "en une heure", faisant de nombreux déçus. Seule information sur le programme de cette soirée: la participation de la chanteuse Monroe.
Pour cette visite apostolique, un accent particulier est mis sur les jeunes, dont le regain de baptêmes en France intéresse particulièrement le souverain pontife, dans un contexte de sécularisation en Europe.
12.000 bénévoles inscrits à Paris
En marge du programme officiel, les adolescents (de 13 à 17 ans) sont conviés sur le parvis de la Défense le samedi 26 au matin, pour un rassemblement festif (mais sans Léon XIV). Les 10.000 jeunes attendus gagneront ensuite la place de la Concorde et les Champs-Élysées pour assister à la messe du pape.
La messe est l'événement phare de l'étape parisienne, pour lequel 400.000 personnes sont déjà inscrites. Les réservations sont gratuites, mais recommandées car elles permettent de faciliter l'organisation de cet événement hors-norme.
Décidé au printemps, organisé en un temps record, l'événement reposera aussi sur les bénévoles: 12.000 sont déjà inscrits à Paris (sur 15.000 attendus), 1.100 à Metz et 2.000 à Lourdes.
Car à Lourdes, où le pape célèbrera une messe le dimanche 27 à 11h sur la prairie du Sanctuaire, les préparatifs s'intensifient aussi: "On est à 115.000 inscrits, ça ne fait que monter. On s’approche très vite de la jauge maximale des 150.000", dit David Torchala, directeur de la communication du sanctuaire, qui se dit "surpris par l’engouement".
Un défi "énorme"
Douze kilomètres de barrières, 1.500 prêtres distribuant la communion... "Tout le gazon sera occupé par les pèlerins", ajoute David Torchala, qui convient que le défi est "énorme".
Pour l'occasion, le Sanctuaire a décidé de recouvrir totalement les mosaïques du prêtre slovène Marko Rupnik, accusé d'agressions sexuelles, qui ornent la façade de la basilique. "L’idée est de pouvoir les maintenir couvertes après le départ du pape", explique le directeur de la communication du sanctuaire.
Car c'est à Lourdes que Léon XIV rencontrera des victimes de violences sexuelles dans l’Église. En 2021, un rapport avait estimé à 330.000 le nombre de victimes mineures en France depuis 1950.
C'est aussi à Lourdes, devant des malades, que Léon XIV parlera de la fin de vie, lors du voyage placé sous la devise "Pour que le monde ait la vie". Le sujet a largement mobilisé l’Église en France, alors que le Parlement votait un texte sur l'aide à mourir.
Le pape se rendra enfin le lundi 28 septembre à Metz (Moselle), où est enterré Robert Schuman, l'un des pères de la construction européenne, et dont l’Église a entamé le procès canonique en vue de sa béatification.
Il adressera là "un message de paix, d’amitié entre les Nations et de réconciliation entre les pays", dit Mgr Bertrand. "Un appel d’autant plus fort qu'il sera lancé en présence du président de la République (et) de ses homologues européens".

title: Nursing mothers on dumpsites: A timely rescue
content:
FOR the downtrodden and hopeless, help can sometimes arrive from the most unexpected quarters. Such a heartening intervention occurred recently when government agents rescued four nursing mothers and their babies from an illegal dumpsite in Agboju, on the Lagos-Badagry Expressway in Lagos State.
Yet, the heartwarming rescue also exposes the disturbing depth of poverty and social vulnerability in Nigeria.
The World Bank says more than 140 million Nigerians live in extreme poverty, aggravated by the removal of petrol subsidies in May 2023.
This is a wake-up call that environmental sanitation cannot be divorced from the human suffering taking place in the very spaces authorities routinely seek to clear.
The Lagos Environmental Sanitation Corps, popularly known as KAI, said the women were rescued on Monday during an ongoing inter-agency cleanup of the Lagos-Badagry Expressway corridor.
According to the Corps Marshal of the agency, Olaniyi Cole, the women were found living in shanties within illegal dumpsites in what he described as inhumane conditions. They were subsequently taken for medical assistance.
The women were identified as Fareedat Muyideen, 23, from Kwara State, who had her two-year-old baby with her; Ayomide Ayomoke, 25, from Ondo State, with her 10-month-old baby; Oziema Abalihi, 20, from Anambra State, with her nine-day-old baby; and Chisom Ugo, 24, from Imo State, with her 11-month-old baby.
Their ages tell a story of their own. They are young mothers, apparently drawn to Lagos by the often-illusory promise of a better life in Nigeria’s commercial capital.
Yet, the fact that a new mother could be living with a nine-day-old infant in an illegal dumpsite should shock the conscience of a country that claims to be committed to protecting its most vulnerable citizens.
It is not enough to see these women simply as violators of environmental regulations or illegal occupants of a dumpsite. Their presence there is symptomatic of a much deeper crisis involving poverty, unemployment, homelessness, family breakdown, migration and the failure of social protection systems.
Cole said the women were living amid filth, poor air quality and hunger. He explained that the rescue became necessary to prevent loss of life, particularly after the condition of one of the newborns was discovered.
The agency has said it is working with relevant authorities to rehabilitate and reintegrate the women into society. That intervention is commendable. But it must not end with rescue.
Rescuing mothers from dumpsites is necessary. Preventing mothers from ending up there in the first place is the real test of governance.
The government must ask what circumstances drove these young women to such an environment in the first place, and what will happen to them after they leave the custody of the authorities.
If they are returned to the same conditions that initially pushed them to scavenging, the cycle will continue. Tomorrow, another group of desperate mothers and children could be found in another dumpsite.
Scavenging in Nigeria is largely an informal survival economy driven by extreme poverty, unemployment and the absence of decent alternatives.
Although available studies differ considerably by location and methodology, they provide a disturbing picture of the people who depend on waste picking.
Research at the Gosa dumpsite in Abuja and multiple sites in Osun and Ekiti states, for instance, has found that between 77 per cent and 100 per cent of scavengers are male.
The studies also show that the activity is predominantly youth-driven, with the average age of waste pickers across various studies put at 27 years. The vast majority are between 12 and 45 years old.
Migration is another important factor. A recent study published in PubMed found that 96 per cent of scavengers in specific urban dumpsites migrated from northern Nigeria due to regional economic pressures.
These figures demonstrate that scavenging is not merely an environmental issue. It is also a poverty, employment, migration and social welfare issue.
Women, children and displaced persons are particularly vulnerable within this informal economy.
Studies across different urban centres have documented women’s participation in waste picking, describing it in some cases as a survival strategy amid urban poverty, unemployment, gender inequality, informal-sector insecurity and environmental injustice.
Thus, while some studies find male dominance in particular dumpsites, the broader evidence shows that women also depend heavily on waste picking in several Nigerian cities.
Mothers and infants living beside decomposing waste can be exposed to toxic smoke, methane, contaminated materials, infectious agents and dangerous air pollution.
Pregnant women and nursing mothers should not be forced to raise children in environments where survival itself becomes a daily battle against hazardous waste.
A 2023 investigation by Premium Times documented the plight of dozens of women scavenging at a dumpsite in Odonla, in the Ikorodu area of Lagos State.
The women reportedly used tablespoons to dig through piles of waste in search of metal scraps. Some rested on tattered rice sacks while toddlers slept beside them.
From dawn to dusk, they searched for scraps to exchange for money. Some bought smaller metal scraps from people who had purchased truckloads of waste containing larger pieces of iron.
The women sometimes paid as little as N8,000 for the smaller metals and employed others to help sort through the waste. In some cases, workers were paid only N1,000 for two to three days of work, with lunch provided.
Some scavengers also pooled resources to buy truckloads of scrap and share whatever profit they made. Sometimes, they made no profit at all.
This is the economics of desperation. No sane person would choose to spend hours digging through foul-smelling waste with a tablespoon if decent employment, affordable housing and social protection were readily available.
Many of these women reportedly regard scavenging as dirty and demeaning, but economic hardship leaves them with few choices.
The government must therefore stop treating the symptoms while ignoring the disease. Periodic demolition of shanties and clearance of illegal dumpsites may improve the physical environment, but without corresponding social intervention, such operations merely displace vulnerable people from one location to another.
Environmental sanitation must be accompanied by rehabilitation, skills acquisition, temporary shelter, healthcare, childcare and pathways into decent employment.
The Lagos State Government deserves commendation for rescuing the four women and providing medical attention. But the state should go further by establishing a structured mechanism to identify vulnerable women and children found during sanitation operations and link them with social welfare services.
The Federal Government, too, has a responsibility. Nigeria cannot continue to preach economic prosperity while millions of citizens remain trapped in informal and hazardous occupations to survive. The expansion of social safety nets, affordable housing, vocational training and employment opportunities must become more than policy rhetoric.
Families must examine the conditions that force young people into the streets. The law should take its course in cases of abuse, neglect or exploitation.
The four nursing mothers rescued in Agboju must not become another fleeting news story. Their rescue should be the beginning of a sustained intervention that addresses not only where they were found, but why they ended up there in the first place.

title: ‘ChatGPT para adolescentes’: Así es la nueva IA que lanzó OpenAI con filtros de seguridad
content:
La empresa de inteligencia artificial (IA) OpenAI anunció este martes el lanzamiento global de ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ (ChatGPT para adolescentes), una nueva modalidad en la que el chatbot limita automáticamente ciertas conversaciones para proteger mejor a usuarios jóvenes y ofrece controles parentales.
Según la compañía, este nuevo chatbot tiene las mismas capacidades que el tradicional, pero está “diseñado para ayudar a los adolescentes a aprender, resolver problemas y explorar nuevas ideas”.
Además, limitará las conversaciones de alto riesgo relacionadas con autolesiones, violencia, trastornos alimentarios y contenido sexual explícito o gráfico.
En algunos casos, ChatGPT enviará alertas a los adultos que hayan optado por activar los controles parentales y las notificaciones.
¿Cómo funcionarán los controles parentales en ChatGPT?
No obstante, los controles parentales no permiten que el padre o el tutor lea o supervise las conversaciones del adolescente.
“Si OpenAI envía una notificación de seguridad, solo comparte la información necesaria para proteger el bienestar del joven”, precisa el comunicado.
También ofrece “recordatorios de tareas” que pueden sugerir el uso del modo de estudio y ayudar a completar las asignaciones paso a paso, en lugar de proporcionar la respuesta en la primera consulta.
Para activar esta nueva función, la empresa rastrea más de 2 mil señales, como los horarios habituales de inicio de sesión, para detectar si un usuario es menor de 18 años, en cuyo caso el chatbot activará automáticamente este modo adolescente.
OpenAI enfrenta críticas sobre riesgo de la IA en jóvenes
Este lanzamiento con enfoque educativo y de seguridad llega en un momento en el que OpenAI se enfrenta a una presión cada vez mayor sobre la salud mental y el desarrollo de sus usuarios más jóvenes.
Grupos de padres en ciudades como Nueva York y Los Ángeles están presionando a las escuelas para que detengan la implementación de productos de IA por temor a que obstaculicen el pensamiento crítico.

title: Jubiläum in Kriegszeiten - Ukraine feiert 35 Jahre Unabhängigkeit - Merz lobt Mut der Bevölkerung
content:
Russland müsse durch die Einheit der internationalen Gemeinschaft in die Knie gezwungen werden, sagte Selenskyj in einer Videoansprache. Sein Land habe im Kampf gegen den Agressor Russland bereits Aufgaben bewältigt, die anfangs unüberwindbar erschienen seien. Der russische Präsident habe unterschätzt, wie entschlossen die Ukrainer für ihre Souveränität kämpften. Selenskyj betonte, die Ukraine wolle unbedingt Frieden, sei aber nicht bereit, sich einfach zu ergeben. Er lobte auch die USA unter Präsident Trump. Die Vereinigten Staaten hätten verstanden, dass Putin den Krieg nicht beenden wolle.
Europäische Spitzenpolitiker in Kiew
Zum ukrainischen Unabhängigkeitstag sind auch mehrere europäische Spitzenpolitiker in Kiew - unter anderen EU-Ratspräsident Costa, Moldaus Präsidentin Sandu, Luxemburgs Premierminister Frieden und Estlands Präsident Karis. Auch der britische Premier Burnham traf zu seinem ersten Auslandsbesuch seit seinem Amtsantritt in der ukrainischen Hauptstadt ein. Dort will er unter anderem mit Selenskyj zusammenkommen und gemeinsam mit anderen internationalen Vertretern an einem Video-Treffen der sogenannten Koalition der Willigen teilnehmen.
35 Jahre Unabhängigkeit von der Sowjetunion
Die Ukraine erlangte ihre Unabhängigkeit im Jahr 1991 von der Sowjetunion nach deren Zusammenbruch. Am 24. August erklärte das Parlament in Kiew die Ukraine zu einem unabhängigen und demokratischen Staat. In einem Referendum stimmten danach 90 Prozent der Menschen im Land dem Beschluss zu.
Inzwischen verteidigt das Land seine Souveränität mit Hilfe westlicher Staaten in dem seit viereinhalb Jahren andauernden russischen Angriffskrieg, bei dem Kiew die Kontrolle über große Teile seines Staatsgebiets verloren hat. Der Krieg hat Millionen Menschen zur Flucht gezwungen und Städte und Dörfer vor allem im Osten und Süden des Landes verwüstet.
Kanzler Merz: "Ukrainer zeigen der Welt, was es heißt, für Freiheit einzustehen"
Bundeskanzler Merz würdigte die Widerstandskraft der Ukrainer in einem Video auf der Plattform X. Diese zeigten der gesamten Welt, was es heiße, für Freiheit und für einen gerechten Frieden einzustehen.
Bundesaußenminister Wadephul - gerade von einem Ukraine-Besuch zurück - rief deutsche Städte und Gemeinden dazu auf, das Land stärker zu unterstützen.


Im Deutschlandfunk sagte er
, es gebe manches Gerät wie Stromerzeuger oder Wasserbehälter, das den Menschen helfen würde, gut über den Winter zu kommen – trotz der gezielten Angriffe Russlands auf die Infrastruktur des Landes. Die EU und Norwegen kündigten unterdessen weitere Milliardenhilfen für das Land an.

Diese Nachricht wurde am 24.08.2026 im Programm Deutschlandfunk gesendet.

Dọc tuyến đường trung tâm, sắc đỏ cờ Tổ quốc phủ kín dòng người, hòa cùng tiếng kèn, trống và những tiếng hô vang "Việt Nam vô địch". Không khí sôi động đã biến thành phố bên sông Hàn thành một đêm hội bóng đá đầy cảm xúc.
Tại Nha Trang, đường Trần Phú rực đỏ trong dòng người xuống đường ăn mừng. Tiếng còi xe, loa phát bài "Như có Bác Hồ trong ngày vui đại thắng" hòa cùng tiếng hô "Việt Nam vô địch".
Nhiều du khách nước ngoài cũng hòa vào không khí cuồng nhiệt trên phố.
Anh Quốc Bảo (24 tuổi, phường Nha Trang) cho biết đã chuẩn bị cờ, kèn từ chiều để xuống đường mừng chiến thắng.

title: Waiyaki family loses fight for Nyari apartments
content:
The family of former Foreign Affairs minister Munyua Waiyaki has been ordered to surrender four apartments in Nyari it unlawfully took from buyers before renting them out during a protracted dispute.
Rosslyn House Ltd and Rosslyn House Management Ltd, which are co-owned by the former minister’s kin, have been ordered to surrender the four apartments to their buyers, who had paid for the units in full.
Arbitrator Peter Njeru ruled that the two Rosslyn House firms had no right to hand possession of the apartments to Tribe Hospitality Solutions Ltd for letting to members of the public, without consent of the apartment owners.
“RW1 (Elizabeth Waiyaki) had emailed the claimants confirming that they were "free to occupy" the apartments. Her evidence that "they had access" and "were free to do so" is incompatible with the respondents’ subsequent change of locks. The respondents spoke with two voices. The argument is also inconsistent with RW1’s express admission in cross examination that the Respondents took possession without the Claimants’ consent,” Mr Njeru said in his decision.
The arbitrator also ruled against the Rosslyn House firms in their decision to change earlier agreed terms which allowed apartment owners to live in their units.
Mr Njeru further faulted Rosslyn House Ltd and Rosslyn House Management Ltd for dumping Tamarind Group as the development’s manager and replacing it with Tribe Hospitality Solutions.
Tribe Hospitality Solutions let the four apartments to the public for a period of four months. The Rosslyn House firms have been ordered to disclose how much rental revenue was made during the unlawful letting of the apartments, triggering a fresh dispute.
The Waiyaki family-associated firms claim to have collected Sh2.1 million in 20 months, which would mean that each unit was let for an average of Sh26,000 per month.
Saveeta Resorts, Mira Hill Ltd and Paramamba Ltd have disputed the figures, arguing that they are inconsistent with rent prices in the upmarket Nyari suburb.
Some terms of the agreement between the Rosslyn House firms and Tribe Hospitality Solutions were kept from apartment owners, which the arbitrator also held was unfair.
“A party cannot be bound by the terms of a contract the material commercial terms of which it has not been permitted to see. Redaction in that context offends basic principles of consent, of the right to information, and of contract formation. In my considered view, the point is elementary: no party is bound by secret terms,” Mr Njeru ruled.
The apartments are in Enaki town, a 22-acre residential resort within Nyari in Nairobi County.
Saveeta Resorts Ltd purchased one unit in 2015 and another in 2022. Mira Hill Ltd and Paramamba Ltd each bought one unit in 2015.
The unlawful possession of the apartments is among multiple disputes that the three buyers have had with Rosslyn House Ltd and Rosslyn House Management Ltd since 2015.
In arbitration, all the disputed matters have so far been ruled in favour of Saveeta Resorts, Mira Hill Ltd and Paramamba Ltd.
Through Rosslyn House Ltd, the Waiyaki family and other investors developed the apartments within their Enaki town, for a reported Sh10 billion.
The residential resort was designed for 450 housing units, a 6.3-acre spiritual garden and several other amenities. The housing units were to be purchased through an off-plan model.
When the project kicked off, Rosslyn House Ltd told buyers that the property would be managed by Tamarind Management Ltd – a subsidiary of hospitality collective, Tamarind Group – for at least the first seven years after completion.
The apartments were initially named in contracts as Tamarind Tree Suites Rosslyn.
The manager would be allowed to lease apartments to third parties, but only after entering into a contract with the unit owners.
Delays in completion of the project triggered the first dispute between Rosslyn House Ltd and Saveeta Resorts, Mira Hill Ltd and Paramamba Ltd. The dispute was, however, resolved with Rosslyn House Ltd eventually discounting each unit from Sh22.5 million to Sh18 million.
After completing construction and handing the units to their owners in 2022, the Rosslyn House firms kicked Tamarind Management Ltd out, and replaced it with Tribe Hospitality Solutions Ltd, which is part of the group that operates the Tribe Hotel and Trademark Hotel. Following that change, the development was renamed Trademark Suites at Enaki. The change, however, triggered a second dispute with Saveeta Resorts, Mira Hill Ltd and Paramamba Ltd.
The three buyers argued that Tamarind managing the property was among the factors that convinced them to invest in the Nyari apartments.
The three buyers said that they have other units at Tamarind Village in Mombasa, managed by the same group to their satisfaction, hence one of the reasons they bought into the Nyari project.
The change of management, the buyers argued, was done without their consultation or consent. Terms of the agreement between the Rosslyn House firms and Tribe Hospitality Solutions Ltd were withheld from buyers.
Additionally, Rosslyn House Ltd and Rosslyn House Management Ltd introduced changes to the operation model.
Under the Tamarind Management Ltd model, buyers had three options – live in the unit, rent it out directly, or hire Tamarind Management Ltd to let the apartment out on the buyer’s behalf in return for a commission.
But under the Tribe Hospitality Solutions model, apartment owners were only allowed to spend a maximum of 14 nights a year in the units they purchased.
Tribe Hospitality Solutions was to take control of marketing and letting the apartments. The rental revenue would then be pooled together and shared amongst owners.
In January, 2023, Saveeta Resorts, Mira Hill and Paramamba requested Rosslyn House and Rosslyn House Management to share leases for signing, with reminders sent in February and May, 2023.
Rosslyn House only sent the draft leases 14 months later, in March 2024.
The Rosslyn House firms also sent redacted copies of the master service agreement they had entered with Tribe Hospitality Solutions, a move that kept apartment buyers in the dark about the deal between those parties.
Shortly after, the Rosslyn firms forcefully took possession of control of the four apartments bought by Saveeta Resorts, Mira Hill and Paramamba and handed them over to Tribe Hospitality Solutions.
At this point, the apartment buyers had not signed the leases, meaning the leases had not been registered with the Lands ministry.
Tribe Hospitality Solutions then changed the door locks and started renting the four apartments to members of the public, triggering a fourth dispute.
Saveeta Resorts, Mira Hill and Paramamba did not know that their units had been rented out, until March 9, 2025 when one of their Directors, Dilesh Bid, visited the apartments and discovered that the locks had been changed.
As they protested to the Rosslyn House firms and Tribe Hospitality Solutions, the three owners filed a complaint with the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI).
They also filed the arbitration case.
The Rosslyn House firms wanted an alternative to be allowed to sell the apartments to other parties and then refund Saveeta Resorts, Mira Hill and Paramamba . But Mr Njeru declined.
“In my considered view, that proposal is not open to the respondents unless accepted by the claimants which they have not. The respondents sold the apartments to the claimants. The claimants paid the entire purchase price. The claimants are the beneficial owners. The respondents cannot resell the claimants’ own apartments over their heads and substitute a refund for the apartments themselves unless of course they are instructed by the claimants to do so,” the arbitrator said.

title: Journalism Can Help Expose Bad Science And Trigger Real-World Change, New Study Shows
content:
Thank you for reading this article: By supporting science journalism, you're also supporting higher standards in scientific research – which benefits us all.
A new study published in Media and Communication looks at the practice of watchdog science journalism, where journalists investigate issues such as malpractice, fraud, and corporate manipulation in scientific research.
Journalism researchers Michele Catanzaro and Luiz Peres-Neto from the Autonomous University of Barcelona in Spain spoke to 15 science journalists across the Ibero-American region (Spain, Portugal, and Latin America).
Journalists in the region have tended to avoid controversial issues, but not those Catanzaro and Peres-Neto interviewed for this study.
Most were able to point to positive, real-world impacts of their work, including changes in regulations, admissions of wrongdoing, organized protests, and increased transparency.
But it's not all good news. The interviewees also talked about struggles with funding, time pressures, and political interference.
"Faced with a systemic problem, the solution also has to be systemic," says Catanzaro.
"Watchdog science journalism is part of it, as it acts as a disincentive to bad practices."
The new findings here chime with earlier research into the same topic that has talked about investigative journalism being a "custodian of conscience".
Investigations were sparked by access to insider information, the 15 study participants said, as well as official documents, academic conferences and events, tips from readers, and resources such as Retraction Watch – a site that maintains a list of papers that have been published and then pulled.
Specific examples of work that the reporters referenced included sexual harassment in Argentine research centers, interference from tobacco and pharmaceutical companies in Latin America, and affiliation purchasing (to artificially boost the standing of a university) in Saudi Arabia.
"The work of these professionals points to a change in Ibero-American journalism, which historically has had weaker traditions of investigation and coverage of science compared to other regions of the world," says Peres-Neto.
Highlighting the importance of watchdog science journalism, the study also captures the challenges journalists face in pursuing these stories. These can include psychological strain, hostility from scientists, and even censorship.
The journalists Catanzaro and Peres-Neto interviewed are also aware that criticisms of scientific research and the exposure of bad practices may erode overall confidence in science more generally – and give more credence to 'anti-science' viewpoints.
"While watchdog science journalism can play an essential role in tackling these issues, it also risks providing ammunition to stakeholders who promote political or corporate interests contrary to scientific evidence," the researchers explain in their published paper.
However, the investigative science journalists interviewed for the study described strategies they use to prevent anti-science uses of their work, such as helping readers to understand how the scientific process works and making sure to properly contextualize erroneous results.
The researchers also have some suggestions about how the long-term future of watchdog science journalism can be ensured.
Giving journalists the opportunity to undertake science-specific training, for example, so they are more familiar with and can scrutinize the institutions and systems that deliver scientific research.
Catanzaro and Peres-Neto are also calling for a broader range of funding sources for this type of journalism and for improved support for staff reporters, editors, and freelancers. That might include granting journalists more time in busy newsrooms to pursue in-depth reporting that takes days, weeks, or years to complete.
Scientific data and discoveries should continue to be made more transparent and accessible, the researchers suggest, through increased accountability at multiple levels: individual researchers, academic institutions, and governments.
After all, so much research is publicly funded.
While only a small number of journalists were interviewed for the study, their experiences parallel those of investigative journalists working in the UK and Canada who, in another recent study, described the legal risks of their work.
"The feasibility of potential stories sometimes plays a bigger role in whether they are reported than their public importance, especially in resource-poor newsrooms," that study concluded.
It's clear that thorough and ethical journalism is vital in maintaining standards in science – something we very much believe in.
Related: These 7 Rules Could Be The Universal Moral Code Shared by Every Culture, Study Finds
"The general perception among interviewees is that their work contributes to triggering changes," write the researchers.
"A large majority of interviewees reported practical impacts of their work, although some said these impacts were not sustained over the long term."
The research has been published in Media and Communication.
This article was fact-checked by Rachel Garner and edited by Clare Watson. While we pride ourselves on our process, we are only human. If you spot a mistake, please let us know.

title: The untold story of Suede’s second act, in their own words
content:
“I couldn’t be more bored by talking about the 90s,” says Suede bassist Mat Osman of the decade when Britpop ruled all and his band, led by Brett Anderson, were at their commercial peak with hits like “Trash” and “Beautiful Ones”. He adds: “There’s just very little interesting left to say. So this seemed like a chance to talk about a very different kind of thing.”
Osman is referring to a new biography by author Rodge Glass, As One: Remaking Suede. It leaves the band’s 90s pomp behind to tell the newer story of Suede’s remarkable and highly improbable second act. Few were grieving when the band split sorrily in 2003 – “it was a relief because we weren’t very good at what we were supposed to be doing,” Osman says – and there was little clamour for their return.
But since tentatively reforming in 2010 for a Teenage Cancer Trust concert at the Royal Albert Hall, Suede have forged an uncommon path forward, rebuilding themselves as a creative force across five albums that peaked with 2022’s Autofiction and last year’s 10th album Antidepressants. Both reached number two in the charts and remoulded Suede into a vigorous post-punk-adjacent band accruing more power with age.
It has raised the band back to a profile and critical acclaim akin to the old days: last month Antidepressants gave Suede their first Mercury Prize nomination in 29 years: fifty-something men looking incongruous in a list alongside today’s pop stars Olivia Dean, Raye and Dave. “It’s really great to be recognised,” says keyboardistguitarist Neil Codling. “We are, to most people’s eyes, a legacy act that they don’t know or care are making new music. But we don’t rest on our laurels and think about ‘Animal Nitrate’ day in day out. We’re like a shark as a band. We need to keep moving forward.”
As One documents with great care and exacting detail how Suede restored themselves from the margins after, as Codling puts it, “the carnival had moved on”. The weight of their history was a well worn tale looming large: Anderson and Osman migrating to London from Haywards Heath in West Sussex; their quick-selling self-titled 1993 debut winning the Mercury Prize with its songs of squalid urban glamour; guitarist Bernard Butler leaving in 1994 while they were making darkly florid follow-up Dog Man Star; 1996’s poppy Coming Up, the first album with Codling and guitarist Richard Oakes, becoming their best-seller; before Anderson’s crack and heroin addictions did for the quality control on 1999’s stranger, colder Head Music.
Codling had left due to illness by the time the dismal A New Morning, from 2002, sealed a miserable falling-off. Having something to prove has been continuous fuel. “Brett in particular really likes and needs to feel like he’s outside something and battling something,” Glass says.
But there is no real precedent for Suede’s creative revival. From The Stone Roses to Pixies, once-great reformed bands invariably struggle to recapture their past glories. It was this aspect that Glass, a Suede fan from the start, was drawn to. “There was such a fascinating story to tell that I couldn’t really believe nobody had got round to,” he says. He’d met Osman at a literary event at Edinburgh Festival (Osman is now an acclaimed author). Osman was a fan of Glass’s biography of Dutch novelist Michel Faber, and in Edinburgh, Glass took the chance to pitch his Suede book idea. It is by no means a hagiography – “I’m critical in places and loving in others,” Glass says – as he was given free rein to interpret as he wished.
“We didn’t want to course-correct,” Codling says. “It’s Rodge’s book. It was that thing, ‘Give me the unvarnished truth, and then I come to my own conclusions.’ That seems to me like a modern idea.”
Glass spent three intimate years with the band from 2022. “I expected more resistance, but I was given a staggering amount of access,” he says. He found a band that were “genuine, earnest, incredibly hard-working, self-critical, curious. And open, once trust was there. With Brett, maybe that trust was a little bit slower.” But Anderson felt comfortable enough to be unusually candid, and disclose that he had endured a brief lockdown-period Valium dependency, the panicked withdrawals from which were medicated with antidepressants.
In interviews promoting Antidepressants, Anderson was keen to stress that the music itself acted as a restorative, but chose not to disclose his own recent struggles. “Because that would be the story,” Osman says. “It’s impossible to talk about any kind of drugs and it not get turned into a one-line, clickbait thing. You can call that cynical, or you can call it idealistic. Because a good song or album contains multitudes. Antidepressants is about the power of music, the power of playing live.”
Osman says that he wasn’t aware of the extent to which Anderson was struggling (“you don’t bring that to work”). The band not conversing particularly well is a theme of the book, with the frustrations and tensions that inevitably follow. “We are five people who fail to communicate again and again and again,” adds Codling, who says the band learned things about each other by reading the book. “‘Oh, that’s what you thought?’”
“We all agree on what Suede should be, but there’s always going to be conflicts,” Osman says. A case in point being the fraught making of 2016’s Night Thoughts, revealed for the first time to have stretched the band to their limits. On release, it was decided that it was best to present a united front. “I think we still have that 90s mindset that it’s very difficult to admit to f**king up and your vulnerabilities,” Osman adds.
For Glass, As One is a human story about creativity, and how five disparate characters unite with a common purpose to make something meaningful: “How do you face your own past and also the future without turning into some kind of cartoon, or living in a kind of denial?” The book therefore forensically recounts discussions around process, songwriting and messaging, from the reunion show through each album. “When we were young, we cultivated this mystique that everything we touched turned to magic,” Osman says. “But this is showing that 90 per cent of it is just hard work.”
There have been key decisions that helped Suede renew. After initially struggling to get 2013’s comeback album Bloodsports off the ground – “The first year of stuff that we wrote was not up to scratch,” Codling says – the band’s long-time producer, the battle-hardened Ed Buller, insisted on clearly defined creative roles: Codling and Oakes writing the music, and Anderson the melodies and lyrics. “Ed thought that having Brett write the music, which happened more for Head Music and A New Morning, made Suede sound less like Suede,” Codling says.
A dynamic plays out with Codling and Oakes needing to have Anderson on board before songs get worked on, at times a trying process. “We are all peers – Richard and I aren’t some kind of a clearing house for music that will get Brett to start writing,” Codling says. “It’s more that we just need to be in sync.” It leaves an unusual situation where Oakes and Codling write the music but stay in the background – Codling and Oakes historically do little press – with Anderson and Osman the public face of Suede. Codling smiles. “That’s just the division of labour.”
Oakes’s untold story is the book’s most moving element. As One reveals his struggles with depression after Suede’s split as he came to terms with what he calls “the best and worst thing that ever happened to me”. At just 17, he was thrown in at the deep end, joining the band as a replacement for Butler, and sent straight on an 18-month tour. Being perceived by some, as Glass puts it, as “an imitation of someone else” left scars and an imposter syndrome Oakes carried for decades.
“Looking back on it, [going straight on tour] was possibly a mistake,” Osman says. “Because he had no chance to actually prove himself as a songwriter. He was just playing someone’s parts.” Codling pushes back slightly. “It’s unfair to say that he was just writing someone else’s style until 2022.” But from Autofiction onwards, Oakes asserted himself, with success a clear vindication of his singular talents. “That was really galling,” Osman says. “Both me and Brett thought, ‘F**k, we should have given him free rein much earlier on.’”
Another change has been in Anderson. While he remains starry and fixated over all aspects of “Suedeworld” – the lyrical content, aesthetics and presentation – he has dropped his armour somewhat, and increasingly seeks genuine connection with the audience. “I think he has learned to be more vulnerable, to show self-doubt,” Osman says. “And the live thing has become much more important to him. We used to be, ‘We are rock Gods, and you’re down there looking at us.’ Now he’s always trying to break down the barriers between band and crowd.”
That live feeling played into the directness of Autofiction and Antidepressants, and steered Anderson’s lyrics about middle-aged anxieties over fatherhood, the knottiness of long-term relationships and the disconnect of modern life. “Brett has found a way to write for Suede’s audience in a way that is honest and convincing and new,” Codling says. The key reunion track, 2022’s “She Still Leads Me On”, is proof: a moving, uplifting anthem about Anderson seeking ongoing meaning from the relationship with his mother, who died when he was 21. “Seeing the way people reacted to that song was like, ‘OK, this is actually landing,’” Osman says.
For once, the band doubled down on something that worked rather than taking a left-field turn: a ballet score was scrapped to make Antidepressants. They could be rewarded by winning the Mercury Prize for the second time. Either way, Osman says Suede’s second act recovery isn’t finished. “We’re trying to build. The moment we think, ‘Everyone loves us. We’re great!’ it will all fall apart again.”
‘As One: Remaking Suede‘ is published on Thursday by New Modern

title: Chính thức: Tăng mức chuẩn trợ giúp xã hội lên 540.000 đồng/tháng
content:
Chính phủ vừa ban hành Nghị định 335/2026/NĐ-CP ngày 21-8 quy định chính sách trợ giúp xã hội.
Theo nghị định, mức chuẩn trợ giúp xã hội từ ngày 1-7-2026 là 540.000 đồng/tháng, tăng 40.000 đồng so với mức 500.000 đồng hiện hành.
Đây là mức dùng để tính trợ cấp xã hội hằng tháng, hỗ trợ kinh phí nhận chăm sóc, nuôi dưỡng và các khoản trợ giúp khác tại cộng đồng cũng như cơ sở trợ giúp xã hội.
Những ai được hưởng trợ cấp?
Các nhóm được trợ giúp xã hội thường xuyên tại cộng đồng gồm trẻ em có hoàn cảnh đặc biệt như bị bỏ rơi, mồ côi hoặc không còn người chăm sóc; trẻ em nhiễm HIV/AIDS thuộc hộ nghèo; người đơn thân thuộc hộ nghèo, cận nghèo đang nuôi con dưới 16 tuổi.
Ngoài ra còn có người cao tuổi thuộc hộ nghèo không có người phụng dưỡng hoặc không có điều kiện sống tại cộng đồng; người khuyết tật nặng, đặc biệt nặng; trẻ dưới 3 tuổi thuộc hộ nghèo, cận nghèo ở địa bàn đặc biệt khó khăn và người nhiễm HIV/AIDS thuộc hộ nghèo không có nguồn thu nhập ổn định theo quy định.
Một số trường hợp đủ 16 tuổi nhưng vẫn đang học liên tục chương trình giáo dục phổ thông, giáo dục thường xuyên, giáo dục nghề nghiệp hoặc đại học văn bằng thứ nhất cũng được tiếp tục hưởng trợ cấp đến khi kết thúc việc học.
Mức trợ cấp tính thế nào?
Trợ cấp hằng tháng được tính bằng 540.000 đồng nhân với hệ số tùy từng nhóm đối tượng.
Chẳng hạn, trẻ em thuộc diện bảo trợ xã hội dưới 4 tuổi được hưởng hệ số 2,5, tương đương 1,35 triệu đồng/tháng. Người từ 4 tuổi trở lên thuộc nhóm này hưởng hệ số 1,5, tương đương 810.000 đồng/tháng.
Người khuyết tật đặc biệt nặng hưởng hệ số 2, tương đương 1,08 triệu đồng/tháng; trẻ em hoặc người cao tuổi là người khuyết tật đặc biệt nặng hưởng hệ số 2,5, tương đương 1,35 triệu đồng/tháng.
Người cao tuổi thuộc hộ nghèo không có người phụng dưỡng được hưởng hệ số 1,5 nếu từ 60 đến dưới 75 tuổi và hệ số 2 nếu từ 75 tuổi trở lên. Trường hợp đủ điều kiện nhưng không thể sống tại cộng đồng và có người nhận chăm sóc tại cộng đồng được hưởng hệ số 3.
Trường hợp một người thuộc nhiều nhóm được hưởng trợ cấp thì về nguyên tắc chỉ hưởng mức cao nhất. Riêng người đơn thân nghèo nuôi con đồng thời thuộc một số nhóm đối tượng khác được hưởng cả hai chế độ theo quy định.
Nghị định cũng quy định người thuộc diện trợ giúp xã hội đang học từ mầm non đến đại học được hưởng các chính sách hỗ trợ giáo dục, đào tạo theo quy định.
Nghị định 335/2026/NĐ-CP có hiệu lực từ ngày 5-10-2026, nhưng mức chuẩn mới được áp dụng từ ngày 1-7-2026. Địa phương có điều kiện có thể quyết định mức chuẩn và mức trợ giúp cao hơn mức quy định của Chính phủ.
Các đối tượng đang hưởng chính sách theo quy định cũ được chuyển sang mức tương ứng theo nghị định mới từ ngày 1-7-2026. Chính quyền cấp xã có trách nhiệm rà soát danh sách và thực hiện chi trả theo mức mới.

title: Traffic improvements on Ranches Street: Road capacity increased by 30%
content: The Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) in Dubai has carried out traffic improvement works on Ranches Street, as part of its continuous efforts to develop road infrastructure and enhance the flow of traffic, in line with the urban and traffic growth in the emirate, and raise the efficiency of the road network and the level of services provided to its users. Improvements have cut travel time by up to 30% during peak hours.These improvements come as part of RTA's ongoing efforts to develop the road network in various areas of Dubai and raise traffic efficiency, through the implementation of fast traffic solutions that keep pace with the urban and urban growth of the Emirate of Dubai, thus providing a more smooth and safe movement for road users, in a way that supports the quality of life and keeps pace with the emirate's goals of easy and sustainable mobility.The works on Ranches Street also included the expansion of the intersection by adding a new traffic lane for vehicles heading from Ranches Street to Street (16A). This has contributed to reducing traffic density and cutting waiting queues by 50%. Installing modern light poles has improved traffic safety and provides better night vision for road users.Ranches Street is one of the vital hubs in Al Quoz, connecting Al Khail and Al Asayel Streets, providing direct access to a number of industrial, commercial, and residential areas. title: Game-Master LLMs for Task-Based Role-Play: Supporting the Acquisition of Idiomatic Language in L2 Learning
content: Natural and idiomatic expressions are essential for fluent, everyday communication, yet many second-language learners struggle to acquire and spontaneously use casual slang despite strong formal proficiency. To address this gap, we designed and evaluated an LLM-powered, task-based role-playing game in which a GPT-4o-based Game Master guides learners through an immersive, three-phase spoken narrative. After selecting five unfamiliar slang phrases to practice, participants engage in open-ended dialogue with non-player characters; the Game Master naturally incorporates the target phrases in rich semantic contexts (implicit input enhancement) while a dedicated Practice Box provides real-time explicit tracking and encouragement. Post-session, learners receive multi-level formative feedback analyzing the entire interaction. We evaluated the system in a between-subjects study with 14 international graduate students, randomly assigned to either the RPG condition or a control condition consisting of a traditional AI-led virtual classroom. Results from an immediate post-test show that the RPG group achieved greater gains in both comprehension of the target phrases and their accurate, contextual use in sentences. A one-week delayed post-test further demonstrates that these gains are retained over time, with the RPG group showing a 21-27% improvement, indicating the effectiveness of our approach in supporting longer-term learning. Qualitative survey responses assessing engagement and perceived effectiveness further indicate that the game-based approach provided more practice opportunities and a more natural learning experience. These findings highlight the potential of narrative-driven LLM interactions in vocabulary acquisition.

title: The likely Agoa extension is positive for South Africa’s agriculture
content:
The US Senate supports extending the African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) for another two years. But the process is not yet final. There are further processes to be completed before the bill reaches the US president for his approval.
Positively for South Africa, it remains part of this process, and Agoa continues to benefit various sectors of the its economy.
For South Africa’s farming sector, the US market is important, accounting for just more than $500-million in exports a year, which is about 4% of total agricultural exports of about US$15.1-billion.
The figure may seem relatively small, and others have even argued that South African farmers must focus on China. But the US market remains critical for farmers and agribusinesses in certain value chains, particularly raisins, table grapes, citrus, nuts, and wine.
The desire to expand access to China, and support it, especially under the zero-tariff access provisions of the China-Africa Partnership Agreement for Shared Prosperity, is understandable. But we must view the Chinese market as an addition to the group of countries that offer access to the South African markets, not a substitute for others. That is the posture that the South African farming sector and organised agriculture have maintained, and I think it’s an important approach to these trade dynamics in the current geopolitical context. South Africans do not enjoy the luxury of choosing sides.
Other stakeholders have also questioned the benefit of Agoa in an environment where the US government has imposed tariffs on a range of goods from South Africa and other trading partners. This, again, is another important matter, but it is important that we all realise that the benefits remain quite tangible.
Tariffs and Agoa
You see, without Agoa, South African products exported to the US would typically face an additional tariff of around 3% (depending on the product) on top of the new tariffs, which are at 12.5%, bringing the total to around 15.5%.
This would have placed South African agricultural products at a disadvantage compared to competitors in the American market, such as Chile and Peru. Because of the Agoa benefit, South Africa is now on equal footing with these countries in the U.S. market, at 12.5%.
I must also say, though, that the US has decided to modify its tariffs and exempt some food products, thus easing agricultural trade friction, which is costly to both exporting countries and US consumers. The exempted products include coffee and tea, fruit juices, cocoa and spices, as well as avocados, bananas, coconuts, guavas, limes, oranges, mangoes, plantains, pineapples, various peppers and tomatoes, beef and additional fertilisers.
From a South African perspective, oranges, macadamia nuts and fruit juices benefit from the exemption. The rest of South Africa’s agricultural products currently face a 12.5% import tariff in the US market.
To remind us again of the agricultural economic value of this discussion, in 2025, South Africa’s agricultural exports to the US totalled US$504-million, down 3% from the previous year. This slight annual decline doesn’t suggest that the previous 30% “Liberation Day tariffs” didn’t have a negative impact on the South African agricultural sector; South Africa benefited from substantial exports in the second quarter of 2025, when there was a 90-day pause, and we have plenty of citrus products to export.
Ultimately, Agoa is not the end of the road, and I believe the South African policymakers have previously made that point clear. The idea is to have a formal trade agreement with the US after these uncertain times. But for now, a likely renewal of Agoa, with South Africa’s continued inclusion, is a positive step for agriculture to continue to compete on the same level as other key agricultural exporters to the US market. title: Will personalised mRNA vaccines transform cancer treatments?
content:
Every cancer is different. Because of that, researchers have for decades been working on personalised cancer vaccines designed to make the immune system recognise and attack cancers specific to each individual. The results have been mixed, but now a personalised cancer vaccine has produced positive results in a final-stage trial for the first time.
Moderna announced on 19 August that people who had undergone surgery to remove severe skin cancers, called melanomas, survived longer without the cancer returning or spreading to other parts of the body if they were given a personalised mRNA cancer vaccine in conjunction with another immunotherapy, compared with receiving that immunotherapy alone.
The hope is that this personalised vaccine will work for many other types of cancer. Trials are already underway for certain kinds of lung, kidney and bladder forms of the condition. The other big mRNA company, BioNTech, is also testing personalised cancer vaccines in human trials.
Advertisement
What is a cancer vaccine?
Cancers are caused by cells accumulating mutations to the point where they go rogue and start multiplying out of control. Mutations in proteins that protrude from the surface of cells also make cancer cells “look” a bit different to other cells. This allows our immune system to recognise and kill off many cancers without us ever knowing about it. But some cancers slip through the net – the idea of cancer vaccines is to teach the immune system to recognise them.
How are these vaccines made?
In the case of the Moderna vaccine, called intismeran autogene, a sample of a person’s cancer – a biopsy – is sequenced. It is then compared with their healthy blood cells to identify surface proteins on the cancerous cells that have distinctive mutations. Up to 34 are selected, and mRNAs coding for those proteins are made and put in the vaccine.
What happens next?
The cancer vaccine is injected into muscles, just like with the covid-19 mRNA vaccine. Cells in the muscles then temporarily produce the cancer proteins, triggering an immune response to them.
Why use mRNA vaccine technology?
It is possible to use other kinds of vaccines, but mRNA has two huge advantages: speed and cost. Making protein-based vaccines requires using living cells, which is time-consuming and requires many safety checks. For people with cancer, the faster a vaccine can be created, the better.
What immunotherapy was the vaccine combined with for the trial?
It is a so-called anti-PD-1 therapy consisting of an antibody called pembrolizumab (Keytruda). Many cancers evolve to evade immune attack by putting up a “don’t attack me” sign. Immune cells “read” this sign with the help of a protein on their surface called PD-1.
Blocking PD-1 makes the “don’t attack me” sign invisible to immune cells, so they attack regardless. However, anti-PD-1 treatments work only if the immune system is already trying to attack a cancer, hence the advantage of combining them with a cancer vaccine to provoke that attack.
How well did the combined treatment work?
Moderna hasn’t told us yet. The company has announced only that the results of the phase III trial “demonstrate statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements” in survival times.
The trial involved 1137 people who, after surgery to remove melanomas, were randomly assigned to get both the vaccine and pembrolizumab, or just pembrolizumab. What we do know is that in an earlier trial involving 157 people with melanoma over five years, the combination of the vaccine and pembrolizumab cut the risk of recurrence by 50 per cent and the risk of spread to other parts of the body by 60 per cent, compared with pembrolizumab alone.
When will this treatment become available?
Analysts speaking to the Financial Times say it could be approved next year. But because it is an individualised treatment, scaling up production will be much more complex than with a standard vaccine.
It also isn’t clear yet what the pricing will be – even with the help of mRNA technology, it won’t be cheap. A January report by Reuters suggested it would cost around $200,000 per treatment. No wonder Moderna’s share price is soaring.
Will this work for all cancers?
The hope is it will work for many cancers, but we will have to wait on more phase III trial results to be sure. That said, several other earlier-stage mRNA cancer vaccine trials have produced promising results. In fact, a study last year estimated that on the basis of these results, their potential health benefits could be worth around $75 billion a year in the US alone.
Are there any approved cancer vaccines already?
Not like intismeran autogene. Some sources will tell you there are three approved vaccines for treating cancer: Provenge, BCG and T-VEC.
But Provenge is a treatment that involves removing immune cells from a person’s body, exposing them to a prostate cancer protein, then replacing them. BCG is the tuberculosis vaccine, which just happens to help treat some bladder cancers for reasons we still don’t understand. And T-VEC is a live herpes simplex virus engineered to kill cancer cells.
So only one of the three is a conventional vaccine, and its anti-cancer action is completely incidental.
What about the HPV and hepatitis vaccines?
These vaccines prevent infections by viruses that can cause cancers, rather than targeting cancers directly, which is an even better approach. The HPV vaccine has proved incredibly effective at preventing cervical cancer, for instance.
